Equal weight to LP, NM, and PL families
Lower is better across all 12 tests
Number of columns where approach is best

1. NM pretraining is the reliable core: all leading broad-transfer approaches use NM.
2. midterm+nm → covid19_twitter+nm and the 3-graph merged / 2-task joint model are effectively tied on the balanced score (gap ≈ 0.0002).
3. The 3-graph joint model is the strongest breadth option: it wins 5/12 tests and is much better on PL transfer, but gives up LP performance.
4. covid19_twitter+nm has the best average test rank and remains the strongest simple baseline.
5. PL-only pretraining is uniformly weak. LP-only pretraining specializes in LP and transfers poorly to PL/NM.
6. The final 3-graph run changes graph count, task count, merging/joint training, and augmentation together; its gain cannot be assigned to one design choice.
Important: there are no repeated seeds or uncertainty estimates here, so tiny differences should not be interpreted as statistically meaningful.

• One result per approach/test means there is no estimate of run-to-run variance.
• Test columns differ in difficulty; raw averages favor families with more columns, which is why the dashboard includes balanced score and mean rank.
• Some tests overlap pretraining graph domains. For a strict out-of-domain claim, add a flag for graph overlap and report in-domain vs out-of-domain aggregates separately.
• The experiment matrix is not factorial: the 3-graph result simultaneously changes graph count, task count, merge/joint strategy, and augmentation. Add matched ablations before claiming which ingredient caused the gain.
• ukr_rus_suspended+pl is near chance for every approach and compresses worst-case statistics; inspect it separately rather than using minimum score as the main selector.
